senses: To rend or tear severely; tear badly; rip all over.
ety: From Middle English *berenden, from Old English berendan (“to peel, take off husk”); equivalent to be- + rend.
examples: Then red with ire, her tresses she berent; And weeping hid the beauty of her face:

senses: Someone who scratches.
A piece of equipment used to scratch part of the body to relieve an itch.
An item made of shreddable material (carpet, corrugated cardboard, etc.) designed to be scratched, usually by pet cats.
A scratch card.
A device for cleaning mud etc. from a wellbore.
ety: From scratch + -er.

senses: To buy again, especially to buy something previously sold (or pawned)
ety: From re- + buy.

senses: Having scabs.
ety: From Medieval Latin scabiōsus (“scabious”), from Latin scabiēs (see scabies); partly reinterpretable as scab + -ious.

senses: A Fascist military cadre
ety: Borrowed from Italian squadra. Doublet of squad and square.

senses: One who uses harsh or predatory means to compete.
ety: First attested in the 1670s, from Latin American Spanish barracuda, perhaps from a Cariban word.

senses: To arrange words or items in order of the first (and then subsequent) letters as they occur in the alphabet.
ety: From alphabet(ical) + -ize.
examples: It was almost impossible to locate specific books in the library until we had alphabetized them by the authors' surnames.

senses: Affected with dystrophy
Having brownish acidic waters due to humus
ety: From dystrophy + -ic.

senses: The fiber of this plant, used in rope, fibers, and cloth.
ety: From Spanish abacá, from Tagalog abaka.

senses: An officer who acts as a kind of undersheriff to the governor.
A criminal who is skilled at picking locks and disabling alarm systems.
A man who operates a lock on a waterway.
ety: From lock + man.
examples: I have gone down to vote for a clerk or a lockman; we have pressing letters to go down and vote for a lockman sometimes.
A lockman is appointed for each parish, and acts as deputy or assistant to the coroner.
You see, at the present time a coroner is appointed to a sheading but a lockman only to a parish, so this will bring them both into line.

senses: One's path through life; a lifestyle or behaviour, now especially when seen as traditional.
ety: From Middle English *lif-wei (attested as lifes wege, lives wegas), from Old English līfweġ. By surface analysis, life + way.
examples: And as under colonialism, in most cases ‘traditional’ values and lifeways were treated as a barrier to economic growth and social progress, and were often purposefully eradicated.

senses: The perceived as perceived
That which is perceived in the noesis/noema duality
An obscure and subtle speech.
ety: From Ancient Greek νόημα (nóēma, “concept”, “idea”, “perception”, “thought”).

senses: A person who is enrolled, as in a school.
ety: From enroll + -ee.
examples: Indeed, President Joe Biden signed landmark legislation to reduce drug copays paid by Medicare enrollees, a policy that Republican legislators opposed.

senses: A kind of three-stringed Japanese fretless lute.
ety: From Japanese 三味線 (shamisen).

senses: The process of occurring in a sequential manner; a serial arrangement; a succession.
ety: From serial + -ity.

senses: the closure of shops and offices, typically as a strike.
ety: Borrowed, via Hindi हड़ताल (haṛtāl), from Gujarati હડતાળ (haḍtāḷ), હડતાલ (haḍtāl), literally “locking of shops”.

senses: Spreadable sausage made with liver.
ety: Partial calque of German Leberwurst, equivalent to liver + wurst.

senses: A plant (Garcinia indica) in the mangosteen family with culinary, pharmaceutical, and industrial uses.
ety: From Gujarati કોકમ (kokam) and Marathi कोकम (kokam).

senses: To set upon; to attack.
To commit the first act of hostility or offense against; to begin a quarrel or controversy with someone; to make an attack against someone.
ety: From Latin aggressum, past participle of aggredi (“to attack, assail, approach, go to”), from ad (“to”) + gradi (“to walk, go”), from gradus (“step”); see grade.

senses: An extended charity appeal on the radio
ety: From radio + -thon.

senses: An energy said to lie coiled at the base of the spine and to be released by yoga.
ety: From Sanskrit कुण्डलिनी (kuṇḍalinī, “coiled”).
examples: The physiology of Tantra yoga focuses on the magical numinosity of the male semen, but the experience of the awakening of kundalini is not an exclusively male phenomenon.

senses: Any of several long-bodied mammals of the subfamilies Mustelinae and Ictonychinae, both in the weasel family Mustelidae.
Notably, the European polecat, Mustela putorius.
A base or despicable person; a wretch.
A tubular device used to support lights on a set.
ety: From Middle English polcat, pulkat, of uncertain origin. Perhaps from Middle English *pole, *poule (“hen”), from Old French poule (“hen”) + Middle English cat. Compare English foulmart.
